High phosphorus content in human milk acts as a catalyst for calcium-binding proteins.
The higher protein-to-solute ratio in cow's milk prevents intestinal calcium transport.
Human milk contains a unique water-soluble form of Vitamin D that is absent in cow's milk.
The low lactose content of cow's milk reduces the acidic environment necessary for calcium solubility.
correctOption: Unabsorbed fatty acids in cow's milk bind with calcium to form non-soluble soaps, preventing absorption.
optionExplanations: Human milk fats are easier to digest. In cow's milk, unabsorbed fatty acids react with calcium to form insoluble calcium soaps, which are then excreted in the stool, significantly lowering the net absorption of calcium.
The high phosphorus content is actually found in cow's milk, which is a disadvantage as it can interfere with calcium assimilation, not human milk as the option suggests.
While cow's milk has a higher solute load, the specific mechanism for reduced calcium absorption is related to lipid interaction, not protein-to-solute ratios.
While the text mentions Vitamin D in human milk, the specific reason given for superior calcium bioavailability is related to fat absorption and the avoidance of soap formation.
Cow's milk actually contains less lactose than human milk (50g vs 70g), but the text links calcium absorption specifically to fatty acid binding.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 545 (Book Page): With cow’s milk, unabsorbed fatty acids tend to bind with calcium and prevent it from being absorbed. Although there is less calcium in human milk than in cow’s milk, it is much better absorbed.

category: Describe prevention and control of polio, viral hepatitis A, cholera, typhoid and food poisoning (except Indian epidemiology )
statement: According to standard global surveillance indicators, what is the minimum required rate of non-polio Acute Flaccid Paralysis (AFP) cases that must be detected per 100,000 population under 15 years to certify a country's surveillance system as sensitive?
options: At least 1 case annually
At least 10 cases annually
At least 20 cases annually
At least 0.5 cases annually
At least 5 cases annually
correctOption: At least 1 case annually
optionExplanations: The detection of at least 1 non-polio AFP case per 100,000 children <15 is the standard indicator for a sensitive surveillance system.
10 cases per 100,000 is far beyond the minimum requirement for sensitivity indicators.
20 cases per 100,000 is an unrealistic and unnecessary threshold for standard AFP surveillance sensitivity.
0.5 cases per 100,000 is below the international sensitivity threshold for polio-free certification.
While 5 cases would be very sensitive, the minimum level required for certification standard is 1 per 100,000.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 209 (Book Page): A country's surveillance system needs to be sensitive enough to detect at least one case of AFP for every 100,000 children under 15 — even in the absence of polio.

category: Describe prevention and control of amoebiasis, ascariasis, hook worm infestation (except Indian epidemiology )
statement: In the prevention of amoebiasis, food hygiene is paramount. For communities utilizing sewage-polluted water for irrigation, what is the recommended method for disinfecting uncooked vegetables to remove Entamoeba histolytica cysts?
options: Exposure to UV-C light for 10 minutes
Soaking in a standard chlorine solution for 30 minutes
Washing with a mild saline solution (0.9%)
Rinsing with cold filtered water only
Use of aqueous solution of acetic acid (5-10 per cent)
correctOption: Use of aqueous solution of acetic acid (5-10 per cent)
optionExplanations: Incorrect. While UV may kill some organisms, the specific recommendation for food hygiene in the reference text is acetic acid or vinegar.
Incorrect. Cysts are notoriously resistant to chlorine levels used for water disinfection and likely standard surface disinfection.
Incorrect. Normal saline does not have the disinfectant properties required to kill or reliably remove amoebic cysts.
Incorrect. Simple rinsing is often insufficient to remove adherent cysts from vegetables irrigated with sewage.
Correct. The text recommends 5-10% acetic acid or full-strength vinegar as an effective disinfectant for raw produce against amoebic cysts.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 248 (Book Page): (c) Food hygiene : ...Uncooked vegetables and fruits can be disinfected with aqueous solution of acetic acid (5-10 per cent) or full strength vinegar (1). In most instances, thorough washing with detergents in running water will remove amoebic cysts.

category: Describe prevention and control of deficiency of Vitamin A and D (except Indian epidemiology )
statement: Under the WHO-recommended short-term strategy for preventing nutritional blindness, what is the specific dosing schedule for a child aged 9 months during a routine contact?
options: 300,000 IU annually
100,000 IU every 6 months until age five
100,000 IU as a single dose
50,000 IU every 3 months
200,000 IU every 6 months
correctOption: 100,000 IU as a single dose
optionExplanations: 300,000 IU is an excessively high dose and is not part of the standard WHO preventive protocols for any pediatric age group.
While the 100,000 IU dose is correct for the infant stage, they transition to 200,000 IU after reaching one year of age; it is not 100,000 IU throughout the entire five-year period.
Children between 6 and 12 months (which includes 9 months) should receive 100,000 IU, which is half of the standard preschool dose.
The interval for massive dosing in prevention programs is 6 months, not 3 months, based on the liver's storage capacity.
The 200,000 IU dose is reserved for children older than one year; younger infants receive a reduced dose to prevent toxicity.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 622 (Book Page): The strategy is to administer a single massive dose of 200,000 IU... to preschool children (1 year to 6 years), and half that dose (100,000 IU) to children between 6 months and one year of age.

category: Describe prevention and control of deficiency of Vitamin A and D (except Indian epidemiology )
statement: A 2-year-old child presents with dull, non-wettable corneas and a history of recent measles. On examination, the cornea appears opaque and the child is photophobic. Based on the protocols for managing medical emergencies associated with Vitamin A deficiency, what is the most appropriate immediate treatment plan?
options: Apply topical antibiotic ointment and administer Vitamin D supplements.
Refer for emergency corneal transplant as the first line of management.
Administer 100,000 IU Vitamin A orally once and review in one month.
Administer 200,000 IU Vitamin A orally on two successive days.
Provide dietary counseling to increase intake of golden rice and fish liver oil.
correctOption: Administer 200,000 IU Vitamin A orally on two successive days.
optionExplanations: While antibiotics may prevent secondary infection, Vitamin D does not address the underlying Vitamin A deficiency causing the corneal melting (keratomalacia).
Corneal surgery is contraindicated in the acute phase of active Vitamin A deficiency as the tissue is too soft and necrotic to support sutures; medical stabilization is the priority.
100,000 IU is the prophylactic dose for younger infants; for a 2-year-old with active corneal signs (xerosis/keratomalacia), it is sub-therapeutic.
The presence of corneal xerosis/ulceration is a medical emergency requiring the high-dose therapeutic protocol of 200,000 IU on day 1 and day 2 to stabilize the cornea.
Dietary counseling is a long-term preventive strategy but is insufficient to treat a child already presenting with sight-threatening keratomalacia or corneal xerosis.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 622 (Book Page): Nearly all of the early stages of xerophthalmia can be reversed by administration of a massive dose (200,000 IU or 110 mg of retinol palmitate) orally on two successive days (24). All children with corneal ulcers should receive vitamin A whether or not a deficiency is suspected.

category: Describe prevention and control of deficiency of Vitamin A and D (except Indian epidemiology )
statement: In the metabolic activation pathway of Vitamin D, which organ is responsible for the final conversion of 25-hydroxycholecalciferol (25-HCC) into the metabolically active hormonal form?
options: Liver
Kidney
Skin
Small Intestine
Adipose Tissue
correctOption: Kidney
optionExplanations: The liver performs the initial hydroxylation step, converting Vitamin D3 to 25-hydroxycholecalciferol (calcidiol), which is the major circulating form but not yet the most active hormonal form.
The kidney contains the enzyme 1-alpha-hydroxylase, which converts 25-HCC into 1,25-dihydroxycholecalciferol (1,25-DHCC), the most potent and active hormonal form of Vitamin D.
The skin is the site of initial Vitamin D synthesis, where ultraviolet radiation converts 7-dehydrocholesterol into cholecalciferol, the inactive precursor.
The small intestine is the target organ where the active Vitamin D metabolite (calcitriol) exerts its primary effect by promoting the absorption of calcium and phosphorus.
Adipose tissue acts as a major storage site for the fat-soluble Vitamin D, but it does not participate in the specific enzymatic hydroxylation required for metabolic activation.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 623 (Book Page): It is now known that vitamin D, by itself, is metabolically inactive unless it undergoes endogenous transformation into several active metabolites (e.g., 25 HCC; 1 : 25 DHCC) first in the liver and later in the kidney.

category: Describe prevention and control of amoebiasis, ascariasis, hook worm infestation (except Indian epidemiology )
statement: Why is direct person-to-person transmission from fresh faeces virtually impossible in the case of Ascariasis?
options: Ascaris eggs must be activated by the gastric acid of a secondary intermediate host.
Freshly passed eggs are only infective if they are immediately frozen.
The infective stage is the adult worm, which cannot survive outside the intestine.
The eggs require a period of maturation in the soil to become embryonated and infective.
The eggs are highly fragile and die immediately upon exposure to oxygen.
correctOption: The eggs require a period of maturation in the soil to become embryonated and infective.
optionExplanations: Incorrect. Ascaris is a monoxenous parasite (direct life cycle) and does not require an intermediate host.
Incorrect. Freezing often kills the eggs or inhibits development; they need warmth (24-32 degrees) to mature.
Incorrect. The infective stage is the embryonated egg, not the adult worm.
Correct. This is a fundamental law of soil-transmitted helminths; the eggs are not embryonated when passed and need soil conditions to reach the infective stage.
Incorrect. Ascaris eggs are actually very resilient in the environment, provided there is moisture.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 249 (Book Page): There is no direct person-to-person transmission, or infection from fresh faeces, because eggs passed in faeces need about three weeks to mature in the soil before they become infective.

category: Plot and interpret growth chart for children under 5 years of age (except Indian epidemiology )
statement: In field settings where a child's exact age is unknown, which anthropometric measurement serves as the most effective alternative to growth charting for assessing acute muscle mass reduction?
options: Mid-upper-arm circumference (MUAC) between the ages of one and five years.
Head circumference measurements because they remain static after age one.
Height-for-age index as it is completely independent of the child's actual age.
Chest circumference relative to the head circumference in infants under six months.
Weight-for-age index, as it only requires a single point weight measurement.
correctOption: Mid-upper-arm circumference (MUAC) between the ages of one and five years.
optionExplanations: MUAC is useful in children aged 1-5 because the circumference stays relatively stable in healthy children, making it age-independent for quick screening.
Head circumference is used to track brain growth and is not a primary indicator of muscle mass or acute nutritional status.
Height-for-age absolutely requires the child's exact age to determine if they are stunted relative to the reference population.
While the chest-to-head ratio is an indicator in early infancy, MUAC is the standard age-independent tool for the 1-5 year group.
Weight-for-age requires the child's age to be plotted correctly on a growth chart; without age, the point cannot be interpreted.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 546 (Book Page): Arm circumference yields a relatively reliable estimation of the body's muscle mass... it cannot be used before the age of one year; between ages one and five years, it hardly varies.
